note: Add a complication by copying an entry. organ must be lung, kidney, heart, liver, brain, or vessel. Set glb to a .glb/.gltf path to replace the gross specimen; the cellular scene stays. The viewer does not need a code change for a new entry that reuses an organ.

complications.title: ARDS

views.label: Lungs
views.text: Both lungs. Sepsis injures them from the blood side. Dependent lobes flood and consolidate first.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: The cut face turns dark red and solid as alveoli fill. Aerated lung shrinks to a small anterior volume.

views.label: Alveolus
views.text: Alveolar wall, capillary, type II cells and oedema. Hyaline membranes remain after the fluid recedes.

complications.reversibleText: Often reversible over weeks if the infection is controlled and the lung is protected. Established fibrosis is not.

complications.title: Acute kidney injury

views.label: Kidney
views.text: The kidney swells and the cortex pales. Injury is microvascular and tubular, not a single blocked artery.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Pale cortex, congested medulla. The pelvis is not the site of septic injury.

views.label: Tubule
views.text: Proximal cells lose their brush border, mitochondria swell, and cells slough into the lumen as casts.

complications.reversibleText: Usually reversible if perfusion is restored early. Tubular recovery can take weeks, and some patients are left with chronic kidney disease.

complications.title: DIC

views.label: Microvessels
views.text: Fibrin and platelets occlude small vessels while the tissue downstream pales.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Thrombi sit in the microcirculation. Bleeding and ischaemia happen together.

views.label: Fibrin
views.text: Tissue factor drives thrombin. Fibrin strands trap platelets and shear red cells.

complications.reversibleText: Microthrombi break down once the trigger is controlled. Large-vessel thrombosis and purpura fulminans leave lasting damage.

complications.title: Myocardial dysfunction

views.label: Heart
views.text: The ventricle dilates and the beat weakens. Most of this stunning reverses over days if the sepsis is treated.

views.label: Chamber
views.text: The cavity enlarges and the wall is relatively thinner. Output falls even though the rate rises.

views.label: Myocyte
views.text: Sarcomeres shorten less. Beta receptors fall and mitochondria swell. The cell is stunned, not dead.

complications.reversibleText: Usually fully reversible within 7 to 10 days as the sepsis resolves. The muscle is stunned, not infarcted.

complications.title: Hepatic dysfunction

views.label: Liver
views.text: The liver enlarges. Cholestasis and steatosis are common. Shock adds hypoxic necrosis around central veins.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Nutmeg congestion and yellow fat. Synthetic failure shows up as a rising INR and falling glucose, not only jaundice.

views.label: Hepatocytes
views.text: Plates swell with fat vacuoles. Sinusoidal flow slows. A shrunken necrotic cell does not recover.

complications.reversibleText: Cholestasis and fatty change reverse as the sepsis does. Hypoxic necrosis does not.

complications.title: Encephalopathy

views.label: Brain
views.text: The whole brain is disturbed without a stroke or a mass. Gyri swell slightly. There is no single lesion to find.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Cortex and white matter look almost normal. The failure is functional: flow, barrier and metabolism.

views.label: Barrier
views.text: Tight junctions open, astrocyte end-feet swell, and microglia pull in their processes. Firing slows.

complications.reversibleText: Often reversible once sepsis and sedation are controlled. Some patients keep long-term cognitive effects.

complications.title: Septic shock

views.label: Vessels
views.text: Arterioles dilate and stop answering. Flow slows and plasma leaks into the tissue.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: The tissue is wet. Capillaries are wide and underfilled.

views.label: Endothelium
views.text: The glycocalyx is shed, junctions open, and nitric oxide relaxes the smooth muscle.

complications.reversibleText: Usually reversible with source control, fluids and vasopressors. Prolonged shock leads to multi-organ failure.
